about: The Lobito Corridor register of Africa Project Atlas: projects financed under the corridor's name or on its rail and road spine, with their status and every financing line, each with its source. Kept by hand; see build_lobito.py for the rules.

projects.name: Lobito Atlantic Railway: the Benguela Railway and Lobito's mineral terminal
projects.status_note: Running since January 2024. Its USD 753 m debt package reached financial close in July 2026, about USD 300 m of it drawn in June. Floods cut the line between Lobito and Huambo for about two months from April 2026, and July 2026 was a record month for international cargo.
projects.summary: A 30-year concession, signed in November 2022, to run, maintain and rehabilitate the 1,289 km Benguela Railway from Lobito to Luau on the DR Congo border, and the port's mineral terminal. Owned by Trafigura, Mota-Engil and Vecturis; about 265,000 tonnes carried in 2025, 400,000 expected in 2026.

cost.note: Investment planned in Angola at the 2023 handover, plus up to USD 100 m for the DR Congo section

finance.note: Announced Dec 2024, signed 17 Dec 2025; financial close of the DFC and DBSA package in July 2026, about USD 300 m drawn in June (split between lenders not disclosed).

To the sponsor Mota-Engil Africa, not to LAR, for its LAR investment obligations; may overlap the sponsors' equity.

projects.name: DR Congo railway, Dilolo to Kolwezi, Lubumbashi and Sakania
projects.status_note: The DR Congo signed a 30-year concession for the whole line with Mota-Engil Africa on 26 August 2026, after the Council of Ministers approved the partnership in July. No loan for the works had been announced. Lobito Atlantic Railway already runs trains from Dilolo to Kolwezi under a track-access deal with the state railway, SNCC.

timeline.event: Angola signs the 30-year concession of the Benguela Railway and Lobito's mineral terminal with the Lobito Atlantic Railway consortium of Trafigura, Mota-Engil and Vecturis; it takes over in January 2024.
Angola, the DR Congo and Zambia sign the agreement creating the Lobito Corridor Transit Transport Facilitation Agency, at Lobito.
At the G20 in New Delhi the United States and the EU back the corridor and studies of a new railway into Zambia.
In Brussels the US, the EU, the three countries, the AfDB and the AFC sign a memorandum on the corridor; the AFC is named developer of the Zambian railway.
Giorgia Meloni pledges up to EUR 320 m for the corridor under the Mattei Plan, a week after the G7 summit in Apulia.
The AFC signs concessions with Angola and Zambia to finance, build and run the new line from Luacano to Chingola.
Joe Biden visits Lobito and co-hosts a corridor summit in Benguela; the White House puts US investment along the corridor above USD 4 bn.
After USAID's closure, the US ambassador in Luanda says Washington remains committed and the DFC and EXIM projects stand.
In Rome, Italy's CDP and SACE sign a EUR 250 m loan to the AFC for the Zambian railway.
EU and US experts present studies pricing the rehabilitation of the Dilolo–Kolwezi–Tenke line at USD 400–410 m.
At the Global Gateway Forum the EU says Team Europe has invested over EUR 2 bn in the corridor.
At the EU–Zambia Lobito Corridor Business Forum in Lusaka, the EU and Zambia sign ten agreements worth EUR 200 m.
China, Tanzania and Zambia sign a USD 1.4 bn deal to modernise the TAZARA railway, the Copperbelt's route east to Dar es Salaam.
The DFC signs a letter of interest with Mota-Engil: the DR Congo line may seek up to USD 1 bn from it.
The DFC signs its USD 553 m loan to the Lobito Atlantic Railway, the Biden-era pledge, with USD 200 m from the DBSA; the DFC is reauthorised the next day.
Angola's Council of Ministers reviews the decree creating the Lobito Corridor Development Company (SDCL).
Angola and the World Bank hold the first regional coordination meeting on the corridor in Luanda.
The DR Congo and Zambia join Italy's Mattei Plan, which reaches 18 countries.
The Lobito Atlantic Railway resumes freight with a copper train from the DR Congo, after floods cut the line between Lobito and Huambo for about two months.
Zambia and the United States realign the USD 491 m MCC compact to the corridor.
Financial close of the USD 753 m DFC and DBSA loans to the Lobito Atlantic Railway.
The AfDB approves USD 255 m and a USD 10 m Mattei Plan grant for Zambia's part of the corridor: the railway, the Mwinilunga–Jimbe road, the Jimbe border post.
The DR Congo signs a 30-year concession of the Dilolo–Sakania railway with Mota-Engil Africa.
At the second corridor coordination meeting, in Lusaka, Angola reports 144 project opportunities in its master plan and commits to a one-stop border post at Luau–Dilolo.

governance.name: Lobito Corridor Transit Transport Facilitation Agency (LCTTFA)
governance.what: The three governments' agency, under SADC, to align transit and border rules along the corridor. The AfDB's 2026 package pays to get it working.

governance.name: The 2023 memorandum
governance.what: The US, the EU, Angola, the DR Congo, Zambia, the AfDB and the AFC set out who does what on the corridor and the Zambian railway; the Commission also lists Italy.

governance.name: Lobito Atlantic Railway (LAR)
governance.what: Trafigura, Mota-Engil and Vecturis: holds the Angolan railway and the mineral terminal for 30 years, runs trains into the DR Congo, borrows from the DFC and the DBSA.

governance.name: Africa Finance Corporation (AFC)
governance.what: Developer of the new Zambian railway, with concessions from Angola and Zambia to finance, build, own and run it.

governance.name: Mota-Engil Africa, in the DR Congo
governance.what: Concessionaire of the Dilolo–Sakania railway for 30 years, the state keeping at least 10%; the Congolese railway SNCC keeps passenger rights.

governance.name: Lobito Corridor Development Company (SDCL)
governance.what: Angolan state company in Lobito to coordinate and promote investment along the corridor.

governance.name: Regional coordination meeting
governance.what: The three governments and their funders, convened by Angola with the World Bank; first in Luanda, second in Lusaka on 5 October 2026.
